qualitative_findings: Relative immunity comparisons and condition-dependent transcription context, not importable absolute MIC values. Biosynthetic-gene effects are not independent proof that each product is a direct resistance determinant. Downstream expression effects remain a caveat; the proposed cooperative immunity model is not a direct physical-complex measurement.

10376839.title: Effects of gene disruptions in the nisin gene cluster of Lactococcus lactis on nisin production and producer immunity.

qualitative_findings: MrsR2/K2-associated susceptibility changes accompany reduced mrsFGE transcription; the transporter route is inferred rather than directly measured.
MrsR1 biosynthesis effects do not establish an immunity determinant in these comparisons. The paper discusses residual transcription, not complete absence.
Binding experiments used modified mersacidin and remain distinct from the native-compound susceptibility evidence.

qualitative_findings: Cinorf10-associated lipid methylation and susceptibility results support the authors' immunity model, but the challenge compound was duramycin, not cinnamycin.
The conclusions propose a regulatory model; they do not directly measure every proposed interaction.
27858169.source_heading_caution: One subheading says cinL; the body and Figure 4 say cinorf10. No cinL synonym is inferred.
27858169.title: A novel mechanism of immunity controls the onset of cinnamycin biosynthesis in Streptomyces cinnamoneus DSM 40646.

qualitative_findings: The study supports transporter-associated self-protection, with distinct secretion and susceptibility effects. Some mechanistic details remain proposed.
Producer, nonproducing laboratory backgrounds and heterologous experiments must remain distinct; neither broad cross-resistance nor species-wide clinical resistance follows.

33106269.title: Secretion of and Self-Resistance to the Novel Fibupeptide Antimicrobial Lugdunin by Distinct ABC Transporters in Staphylococcus lugdunensis.

locations: Drug identity and endpoint definitions, page 286
qualitative_findings: The study explicitly tests nisin A and supports limited NisI-associated protection in a laboratory Lactococcus background. It distinguishes background, donor and derivative identities. Its endpoint is not standardized MIC, and the separately conditioned E. coli comparison must not be collapsed into native resistance. Text extraction misaligns table rows and sometimes confuses nisI with nisZ; use the page images. This study does not establish the later papers' commercial congener or an exact experimental protein.
